divergences.old: jira issue schema --example-only printing the bare example with no envelope
divergences.toil: The flag stays; the example comes back as data in the usual envelope, so with the flag data is the example itself, not { schema, example }. Save .data to use it as an --input-file
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope, so an agent never has to guess which shape stdout holds. The allowed fields are excused only for calls with --example-only (`when`), so plain jira issue schema must still return both.

divergences.old: jira issue download fetching the attachment's content URL, with the token, from whatever host Jira names
divergences.toil: The token goes only to baseUrl's origin: a content URL on another host has its path and query re-pointed at baseUrl, with a JIRA_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning
divergences.why: A server-supplied URL must not carry the user's credential to a host they didn't configure. A change a principle requires, so the integration makes it before a live run (CLAUDE.md, The command contract).

divergences.old: jira issue download reporting saved with the platform's separator
divergences.toil: saved uses forward slashes on every platform; the file lands in the same place
divergences.why: Paths in JSON output are identical on Windows, macOS and Linux (CLAUDE.md, Cross-Platform). On macOS and Linux the separator is unchanged.

divergences.old: jira issue download reporting saved as --dir joined with the file name, so a relative --dir gives a relative path
divergences.toil: saved is always the absolute path written, with forward slashes, even when --dir is relative. The file lands in the same place (#233)
divergences.why: A relative --dir resolves against the workspace, which over MCP is not the caller's working directory, so a relative saved would point somewhere else. The absolute path says exactly where the file is.

divergences.old: jira issue download writing to a file that already exists
divergences.toil: Refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the path; the existing file is left alone. The contract records it being replaced (#70 item 8)
divergences.why: A read-only command, whose file name comes from whoever uploaded the attachment, must not change files already on disk.

divergences.old: jira issue search, issue comments, board list and sprint list paging for as long as the server keeps answering
divergences.toil: Paging stops after 1,000 pages (100,000 items at 100 a page) with an HTTP error naming the list, e.g. "Paging Jira search didn't end after 1000 pages", and a fix to narrow the request
divergences.why: A server that ignores startAt hands back the same page forever; the bound turns a hang into an error that says what happened. A list that size is far past anything a caller can use in one envelope.

divergences.old: jira issue fields --discover typing each field with toilType, the customFields type that suits it
divergences.toil: Each field carries that type as suggestedType, and no second type-hint key. Read suggestedType where toilType was read; the value is the same
divergences.why: One name for one fact: the same type under two keys leaves a caller guessing which one is authoritative, and the two can drift apart. suggestedType says what the value is, a suggestion for a customFields entry.

divergences.old: jira issue download saving the attachment under the name the server gave it, once reduced to its last path segment
divergences.toil: A name Windows reserves for a device (CON, NUL, COM1 and the like, with any extension) is saved with a leading _, a : and everything after it is dropped, as are trailing dots and spaces, and the characters Windows forbids become _. filename in data is still the server's name; saved is where the file went. A --dir that names any of those is refused with INVALID_INPUT.
divergences.why: Windows reads each of those as a different file from the one named: a device, a stream inside an existing file, or the same name without its dots. The no-overwrite check has to see the file a write really lands on, and a name must work the same way on every platform.
